policy: Original core mechanics are authoritative; modern presentation must not change economic outcomes; modern gameplay additions must be opt-in.

mechanics.title: Per-player weekly turns
mechanics.target: One turn per player; week advances after all players finish.
mechanics.current: Turn order supports 1–2 humans and AI; 4-human original maximum unavailable.
mechanics.acceptance: Four humans complete a week in correct order without taking actions for each other.

mechanics.title: 60-hour weekly budget
mechanics.target: Start each player turn with 60 hours, original modifier exceptions recorded.
mechanics.current: Classic uses 60h (Modern retains 40h), hunger penalties still simplified.
mechanics.acceptance: Fresh game starts with 60 hours; no duplicated time deductions; imported games handled by migration policy.

mechanics.title: Movement and building entry
mechanics.target: Distance-based movement; entering a building costs 2h.
mechanics.current: Classic adds 2h per travel entry on top of simplified ring distance; DOS distance is unverified.
mechanics.acceptance: Move around ring, reenter building, track exact expected time with original observations.

mechanics.title: Action time accounting
mechanics.target: Full work session 6h paid for 8h; job application 4h; study 6h; relaxing 6h.
mechanics.current: Classic 4h application and 6h relaxation; work 6h/8h pay, study 6h. Partial-work handling unimplemented.
mechanics.acceptance: Full and partial work, success/failure application and study action charge documented hours.

mechanics.title: Single job, workplace locking
mechanics.target: Exactly one primary job; work only at its workplace; switching replaces role.
mechanics.current: Implemented with explicit switch confirmation.
mechanics.acceptance: Two hired positions never coexist; former employer denies shifts; current one allows work.

mechanics.title: Applications and openings
mechanics.target: Requirements + chance-based no openings; failed applications still consume time.
mechanics.current: Classic now uses the 37-job DOS/floppy catalog, stat/diploma qualification rejection (+4h/-1 Happiness), qualification-sensitive openings chance and same-week rejection lockout; original RNG order still unverified.
mechanics.acceptance: Under-qualified and no-opening attempts use original rejection/time rules.

mechanics.title: Work-stat gains and caps
mechanics.target: +1 experience/+1 dependability per work session up to job/degree caps.
mechanics.current: Classic stat caps now use the DOS 37-job requirement data and completed diploma counts; XP/Dependability capped per authentic role. Work/dismissal edge cases still require DOS comparison.
mechanics.acceptance: Repeated entry-job shifts reach cap, not infinity; changing jobs/degrees affects cap.

mechanics.title: Dependability and firing
mechanics.target: 20 initial, -3 per week; low stat warnings and dismissal on work attempts.
mechanics.current: Classic starts Dependability 20 and decays 3/week; hiring below 10 resets it, low reliability warns, and work attempts below job requirement−5 dismiss without pay. Exact messages/DOS edges unverified.
mechanics.acceptance: Week decay, hire minimum, warning threshold and firing reproduced with seeded results.

mechanics.title: DOS-floppy employment catalog
mechanics.target: 37 original DOS positions with employer, base wage, XP, Dependability, diplomas and uniforms; preserve CD-only distinction.
mechanics.current: 37 documented floppy positions implemented in Classic data; two CD-only jobs omitted; shared modern building venues not 1:1; exact DOS binary comparison pending.
mechanics.acceptance: Every Classic role is tested against the documented table, with no Modern Story catalog changes.

mechanics.title: Wages and raises
mechanics.target: 8h pay for full 6h work, current wage; raise prerequisites, wage changes and risks.
mechanics.current: Classic uses documented $5–$25 base hourly wages, listed-wage raises (+4h) and half-shift garnishment/$2 interest. Original macroeconomy pricing curve and partial shifts remain different.
mechanics.acceptance: Pay matches applied wage, raise refusal/cost, garnishment and role switching exact.

mechanics.title: Eleven branching degrees
mechanics.target: 11 permanent named degrees with prerequisite edges and possible multi-course progress.
mechanics.current: 11 named diplomas and original prerequisite graph now feed 37 DOS job qualifications; course availability/end-condition and original implementation variants still unverified.
mechanics.acceptance: All 11 degrees reachable through correct graph; job-specific combinations enforced.

mechanics.title: Course time and benefits
mechanics.target: Enroll fees and 6h lessons, usually 10 lessons; studies can benefit from durables.
mechanics.current: Classic enrollment $50, ten 6h lessons (1–5h partial final time permitted), computer and three-book study aids, graduation +5 happiness/reliability. Enrollment queue and item details require DOS validation.
mechanics.acceptance: Enroll, alternate courses, complete 10 lessons, adjust for valid aids, graduate.

mechanics.title: Weekly uniform consumption
mechanics.target: Three tiers, weekly wear including unworn; higher tier satisfies lower; budget/premium durations.
mechanics.current: Implemented week-based casual/formal/business clothing with tier substitution.
mechanics.acceptance: An unused outfit ages each week; expired uniform blocks work; superior outfit substitutes.

mechanics.title: Durables and supply market
mechanics.target: Durables have benefits, wear/breakage/theft risks; shops rotate stock.
mechanics.current: Ownable items but limited damage and original stock variety.
mechanics.acceptance: Buying durable modifies right mechanic; breakdown, theft and changing stock reproducible.

mechanics.title: Rent cycle and debt
mechanics.target: Rent due every 4th week; manual payment/extensions; garnishment/arrears consequences.
mechanics.current: Classic cash-paid $325 rent due week 4, four-week billing, extensions, arrears and half-shift wage garnishment with $2 remaining-debt fee. Advanced payments, rental switching, DOS exact timing still partial.
mechanics.acceptance: Choose rent office payment; miss it and observe prescribed arrears, garnishment, extension.

mechanics.title: Weekly food and storage
mechanics.target: Fresh food/fast food choices, perishability, fridge and weekend consequences.
mechanics.current: Classic market has original 1/2/4 fresh-food portions ($55/$100/$190), one weekly use, refrigerator capacity 6 and freezer capacity 12, spoilage of unrefrigerated leftovers. Doctor bill and fast-food menu are still approximations.
mechanics.acceptance: Compare 4-week food inventory with/without fridge; validate spoiled food and week events.

mechanics.title: Bank, loans and investments
mechanics.target: Savings; loans/repayment; investment categories; differing liquid-cash risk.
mechanics.current: Classic separate six-stock broker with documented base prices, $100 deposits/withdrawals, no savings interest, loans and $45 principal+$5 interest payments, defaults. Volatility/credit approval formula and random crash/theft remain approximate/missing.
mechanics.acceptance: Document and replicate loan interest/default, 6 markets, cash theft exposure.

mechanics.title: Pawn, repossession and durable economy
mechanics.target: Pawn valuables, redeem within time window, other players can buy unredeemed goods.
mechanics.current: No equivalent pawn-shop simulation.
mechanics.acceptance: Pawn item, redeem within window, let it expire, other player buys it.

mechanics.title: Economic cycles and random losses
mechanics.target: Events may cause robberies, job loss, weekends; timing differs by DOS edition.
mechanics.current: Classic disables non-original civic modifiers/opportunities; original economic/random event distribution absent.
mechanics.acceptance: Edition-specific seeded economic/robbery weekend events follow original windows and effects.

mechanics.title: Four adjustable goals
mechanics.target: Wealth, happiness, education and career; win when all chosen thresholds achieved.
mechanics.current: Four configurable goals exist, but advancement formulas differ.
mechanics.acceptance: Known reference states produce expected goal scores and victory trigger.

mechanics.title: Education/career scoring
mechanics.target: Education ≈1+9/degrees; career ≈1.25×dependability in secondary reference.
mechanics.current: Classic degree score 1+9×diplomas and employed career score 1.25×Dependability; Modern story keeps tier and linear education scoring. Other goal formulas still simplified.
mechanics.acceptance: Compare all four formula outputs against original observations, including unemployment.

mechanics.title: Optional modern content isolation
mechanics.target: Original rule outcomes must be same with cosmetic/UI modernizations.
mechanics.current: Classic original-style jobs, rent, bank and fresh-food services isolated from Modern Story, whose original 19 jobs, auto-rent, generic investments, savings interest and groceries are unchanged. World era remains cosmetic.
mechanics.acceptance: Classic ruleset suppresses non-original mechanical bonuses while keeping dialog optional.
